_comment: Coalition membership as data, not code (issue #1, story 20; ADR 0001).
party_to_coalition rolls a GE15 ballot party name up to the Coalition it
contested under. Parties absent from this map keep their own bracketed
short code as their Coalition, so a minor party is never silently merged
into a bloc it does not belong to.
government_coalitions is the Government Coalition as of August 2026 and is
the value to edit if the coalition realigns — e.g. DAP's 16 Aug 2026
congress on remaining in PH. Nothing in the Swing Model needs to change.
_aliases_comment: How each Coalition is named in Malaysian coverage, English and Bahasa
Malaysia, including the component parties whose names stand in for the
Coalition in a headline.
Matched case-SENSITIVELY on word boundaries, because every entry is a
proper noun and several are also ordinary Bahasa Malaysia words: pas
('quite'), bersatu ('united'), keadilan ('justice'), amanah ('trust'),
gerakan ('movement'), barisan ('row'), perikatan ('alliance').
For the same reason the bare one-word forms of the Coalition names are
not listed — 'Pakatan' and 'Barisan' alone open the door to sentences
that are not about a Coalition at all. A missed mention only shrinks the
sample; a false one moves a Coalition's score for no reason.
Leaders' personal names are deliberately excluded: coverage of a person
is not reliably coverage of their Coalition.
Reading Malay outlets (issue #13) made two of these wrong, in opposite
directions:
- 'PBB' is gone from GPS, replaced by the party's full name. In Bahasa
Malaysia PBB is overwhelmingly Pertubuhan Bangsa-Bangsa Bersatu, the
United Nations. It scored a Hiroshima anniversary story as GPS
sentiment on the first Berita Harian run. GPS draws few mentions, so a
handful of UN stories would have dominated its score outright.
- 'Umno' joins 'UMNO' for BN. Mixed case is house style at NST, FMT and
Bernama, so case-sensitive matching was already missing most of BN's
strongest alias in English coverage; the Malay papers write UMNO.
Unlike the excluded words, 'umno' is not a word in either language, so
the case rule buys nothing here.
'Pas' and 'Bersatu' stay out for the reason above even though Utusan and
NST use both for the parties: 'pas' is a permit and 'bersatu' is 'united'
— capitalised freely at the start of a sentence, in headline case, and in
company names ('Afijay Bersatu'), all seen in one day's feeds.
